sections.h2: What is Lauderhill like for a seller?
sections.html:
Lauderhill incorporated on June 20, 1959 with about 100 residents and now covers 8.5 square miles in Broward County. Its profile page gives a population of 74,479, a commission and city manager form of government with five elected commissioners, and zip codes 33311, 33313, 33319 and 33351.

The housing stock is described as an abundance of single-family homes, multi-family buildings and townhouses. The city runs a Community Bus Shuttle and received the All-America City award in 2005. Citing Census data, it gives household income at $38,805 for the city and $54,895 for Broward, and median age at 35.9 against 40.1.

Schools named on the profile include Broward Estates, Castle Hill, Larkdale, Paul Turner and Royal Palm elementaries, Lauderhill 6-12 STEM-MED Magnet School, Parkway Middle and Piper High School. Florida Medical Center is the hospital named there, and the page counts about 5,000 registered businesses with 10,475 people employed. The same page puts college-degree holders at 19 percent.

  • Confirm school assignment with the district before naming a school in a listing.
  • Mention the bus shuttle if your address is near a route.
  • State whether the house is single-family, a townhouse or part of an association.

sections.h2: Who signs the deed when a Lauderhill owner has died?
sections.html:
First settle who has legal authority to sign the deed. If the owner died holding the house alone, a court usually has to name a personal representative before a title company will close.

Florida allows summary administration for smaller estates, when countable assets stay at or under $150,000, and also once two years have gone by since death (s. 735.201). A house still counts as real property, so Lauderhill heirs normally need some court step. Creditors get a limited window: the later of three months from first publication of the notice to creditors or 30 days from service on a known creditor (s. 733.702).

  • Gather the death certificate, the will if there is one, and the deed.
  • Ask the Broward clerk what the probate division requires for a house.
  • Pay taxes and insurance on time until the estate closes.

sections.h2: Does an inheritance trigger state estate tax or a deed tax?
sections.html:
No estate tax applies. Florida's ended for deaths after December 31, 2004, and state revenue staff say filing Form DR-312 or DR-313 has been unnecessary since July 1, 2023.

A personal representative's deed under a probated will sits on the state's not-taxable list for documentary stamps. An ordinary sale deed does not: it carries the documentary stamp rate stated in s. 201.02, seventy cents for every hundred dollars of price in Broward, and the signers share liability.

sections.h2: What happens to the homestead exemption and tax cap after a death or sale?
sections.html:
Both reset. Homestead depends on the owner living in the house as a permanent residence on January 1, and renting it out or moving away ends it.

Under Save Our Homes, yearly growth in assessed value stops at 3 percent or CPI, whichever is smaller, and the state's chart printed 2.7 percent for 2026. After a sale or other change of title, the following January 1 brings a fresh valuation at just value (s. 193.155). Heirs who keep and rent the house should expect a higher bill than the decedent's.

sections.h2: What tax dates should a Lauderhill seller watch?
sections.html:
The county property appraiser sets values and approves exemptions, and the tax collector bills. The dates below come from the state revenue calendar.

Property tax steps for a Broward County home
StepTimingOffice
File for exemptionsBy March 1Property appraiser
Proposed tax notice (TRIM)AugustProperty appraiser
Challenge a valueWithin 25 days of the noticeClerk of the court
Tax billsNovemberTax collector
DelinquencyApril 1Tax collector

An unpaid bill on an inherited parcel deserves a call to the tax collector for the exact amount, because the clock toward a June 1 certificate sale keeps moving.

sections.h2: What does Lauderhill's city government post for residents?
sections.html:
The city's own site carries news, events and meetings. In November 2026 it listed a Veterans Day ceremony, a neighborhood district meeting for the Isles of Inverrary and the swearing-in of a new police chief at City Hall.

Neighborhood district meetings show which areas are organized and what is on the agenda, and sellers who attend or read the minutes learn what neighbors are asking the city to fix. For permits, code questions or a certificate of occupancy, call the city before pricing. Unpermitted work that a buyer discovers can slow a closing.

  • Ask whether open permits or code cases exist on the address.
  • Have the title company search for municipal liens.
  • Keep receipts for repairs you complete before selling.

sections.h2: How should heirs compare offers on a Lauderhill house?
sections.html:
Put every offer on one sheet with the same lines: price, repairs the buyer expects you to make, who pays the deed tax, who pays recording, and the closing date. An offer that looks high can lose that lead once those lines are filled in.

Ask whether the buyer closes with no financing contingency, whether a deposit becomes non-refundable, and what happens if the estate needs extra weeks for court paperwork. A cash purchase tends to suit a house the heirs do not want to repair, with belongings inside and family out of state. A listing may bring a higher price when the house is clean and the estate can wait.

Photograph each room before anything leaves, and decide in writing who gets which keepsakes. Disagreements among heirs can stall a closing as surely as a missing document can. Name one heir to speak with buyers and the title company, so that every question gets a single answer.

sections.h2: How should I clear and prepare an inherited house?
sections.html:
Plan the work in a weekend or two. Walk through with a list and sort contents into keep, donate, sell and discard piles. Keep personal papers, tax returns, insurance policies and anything with an account number in a locked box until the estate attorney says what to retain.

Check that utilities stay on, the locks are changed, and the insurer knows the owner has died, since a vacant house can change coverage terms. Mow, remove mail and flyers, and photograph the condition so you can show what the buyer saw.

If the house needs work and no heir wants to manage contractors, an as-is sale shifts that job to the buyer. Get the price in writing and compare it to what a repaired house might bring after months of effort and carrying costs.

faqs.q: Can heirs sell before the estate closes?
faqs.a: Usually not until a personal representative has authority to convey. A probate attorney or the Broward clerk can say whether summary administration fits, which turns on the $150,000 threshold or two years since death.

faqs.q: Does Florida charge estate tax on a house passed to heirs?
faqs.a: No. The state tax ended for deaths after December 31, 2004.

faqs.q: What is the Save Our Homes cap in 2026?
faqs.a: The state chart printed 2.7 percent for 2026. The smaller of 3 percent or CPI sets it, and a sale starts the clock over.

faqs.q: Who pays the deed tax when a Lauderhill house sells?
faqs.a: The signers share liability whichever party the contract names, at seventy cents on each hundred dollars of price in Broward (s. 201.02).

faqs.q: Which schools does the city profile name?
faqs.a: It lists five elementary schools, Lauderhill 6-12 STEM-MED Magnet School, Parkway Middle and Piper High School. Ask the district which one serves a given street.
